MESSAGE:
Hi! I'm organising a half-day community workshop at the library on a Saturday and I'm drowning in logistics.

First, a title for the event. It's about helping small local groups get better at social media, so something friendly.

The room is ours from 09:00 to 14:00, hard stop. Sessions: a 60-minute keynote, a 45-minute panel, a 90-minute hands-on workshop, 30 minutes of lightning talks, and a 45-minute lunch. The keynote speaker can't arrive before 10:00. The panel moderator has to leave by 11:00, so the panel needs to be finished by then. The caterers deliver at 12:15 and the food can't sit around, so lunch has to start between 12:15 and 12:45. The workshop has to come before lunch, and after it we need 15 minutes to reset the room before whatever comes next. Could you lay out a full timetable that works?

Could you also write a two-sentence blurb for the library newsletter? And what's a good colour for the name badges? We're printing on white card. Recommend whether to do registration with a paper sign-up sheet or an online form for a mostly older crowd, and give me three icebreaker ideas that don't involve anyone standing up and talking about themselves. Oh, and one more: could you draft a short thank-you email we can send to attendees afterwards, with a link to a feedback form? Two or three sentences is plenty.

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a friendly event title
2. Lay out a full timetable satisfying all room, speaker, catering and reset constraints  KEY: Any timetable that satisfies ALL: within 09:00-14:00; panel (45) ends by 11:00; keynote (60) starts at or after 10:00; workshop (90) before lunch followed by a 15-min reset; lunch (45) starts 12:15-12:45; lightning talks (30) fit. Only 15 min of slack overall. Valid example: Panel 09:00-09:45, Keynote 10:00-11:00, Workshop 11:00-12:30, reset 12:30-12:45, Lunch 12:45-13:30, Lightning 13:30-14:00. Another: Panel 09:00-09:45, Workshop 09:45-11:15, reset, Keynote 11:30-12:30, Lunch 12:30-13:15, Lightning 13:15-13:45. Scorer: check each constraint; any violation = incorrect.
3. Write a two-sentence newsletter blurb
4. Suggest a name-badge colour
5. Recommend paper sign-up vs online form for registration
6. Give three icebreakers that avoid self-introductions
7. Draft a short post-event thank-you email with a feedback link

ANSWER:
# Community Social Media Workshop: Plan

## Title
**"Social Media Made Simple: A Workshop for Local Groups"**

Alternatives: *"Get Your Group Noticed Online"* or *"Post, Share, Connect: Social Media for Community Groups"*

## Timetable

| Time | Session |
|---|---|
| 09:00 – 09:15 | Arrival, registration & tea/coffee |
| 09:15 – 10:00 | **Panel** (45 min) |
| 10:00 – 11:00 | **Keynote** (60 min) |
| 11:00 – 12:30 | **Hands-on workshop** (90 min) |
| 12:30 – 12:45 | Room reset (15 min) |
| 12:45 – 13:30 | **Lunch** (45 min) |
| 13:30 – 14:00 | **Lightning talks** (30 min) |
| 14:00 | Hard stop |

**How the constraints fit:**
- The panel ends at 10:00, an hour before the moderator's 11:00 deadline.
- The keynote starts at 10:00, as soon as the speaker can arrive.
- The workshop comes before lunch, with the 15-minute reset straight after it.
- Lunch starts at 12:45, the latest allowed time. The food will sit for 30 minutes after delivery.
- The day ends exactly at 14:00.

**This is the only arrangement that works**, apart from moving the 15 spare minutes around. The keynote can't start before 10:00, and the panel must finish by 11:00, so the panel has to come first. After that, keynote + workshop + reset leaves lunch at exactly 12:45. So lightning talks can only go after lunch.

**Risks to watch:**
- **There is no buffer before lunch.** If the keynote or workshop runs even 5 minutes over, lunch slips past 12:45. Give the keynote speaker and workshop lead a firm time-warning signal.
- **The food will sit for 30 minutes.** Ask the caterers whether they can deliver at 12:30, or check that dishes can be kept covered or warm.
- If you'd rather the panel start right at 09:00, you can run it 09:00–09:45 and use 09:45–10:00 as a coffee break instead.

## Newsletter Blurb
Does your club, charity or community group want to reach more people online but isn't sure where to start? Join us at the library on Saturday [date] from 9am to 2pm for a friendly, hands-on workshop with practical tips, expert speakers and lunch included.

## Badge Colour
On white card, use **navy blue**. It's high-contrast, easy to read for older eyes, and looks professional. Print names in large, bold type (at least 28pt). If you want a second colour to mark speakers or volunteers, a deep teal or burgundy stripe works well.

## Registration
**I recommend a paper sign-up sheet at the library desk as the main method.** For a mostly older crowd, it's familiar, needs no email or device, and the library staff can help anyone on the spot. Add a phone number people can call to register. You can still offer a simple online form for those who prefer it. Just keep one master list so you don't double-count.

## Icebreakers (no standing up to talk about yourself)
1. **Post-it wall:** As people arrive, they write "One thing my group wishes more people knew about us" on a sticky note and add it to a wall. You can refer back to the notes during the day.
2. **Table bingo:** Give each table a bingo card with squares like "Has a Facebook page," "Has never posted a video," or "Runs a group with more than 50 members." Tables chat among themselves to fill it in.
3. **Show of hands / coloured cards:** Ask quick-fire questions ("Who has posted something in the last week?" "Who finds hashtags confusing?") and have people raise a hand or a coloured card. It breaks the ice, and you learn the room's skill level.

## Thank-You Email

**Subject:** Thank you for joining us!

Thank you so much for coming to *Social Media Made Simple* at the library on Saturday. We hope you left with some useful ideas for your group. We'd love to hear what you thought, so please take two minutes to fill in our short feedback form: [LINK].

Warm wishes,
[Your name]
